questions.questionText: Which sentence is the negative form of 'She walks to school'?

options.a: She does not walk to school.
options.d: She is not walk to school.

questions.explanation: Present simple negative: subject + does not + base verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is the negative form of 'They played football'?
questions.explanation: Past simple negative: subject + did not + base verb (not past form).

questions.questionText: Which sentence is the negative form of 'She will travel tomorrow'?
questions.explanation: Future negative: will not / won't + base verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is negative? 'She is cooking dinner.'
questions.explanation: Present continuous negative: subject + is/are not + verb-ing.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is the negative form of 'They were sleeping'?
questions.explanation: Past continuous negative: was/were not + verb-ing.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is negative? 'I have visited Paris.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect negative: have/has not + past participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'can' for permission?

options.a: Can I open the window, please?
options.d: Can you help me with this?

questions.explanation: 'Can I...' = asking permission politely.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'could' for polite request?

options.a: Could you pass me the salt, please?
options.b: I could run fast when I was young.

questions.explanation: 'Could you...' = more polite request than 'can you'.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'should' for giving a suggestion?

options.a: You should try the new restaurant.

questions.explanation: 'should' + base verb = suggestion (no -s, no to).

questions.subtopic: Modal verb would past habit basic
questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'would' to talk about past habits?

options.a: When I was a child, I would visit my grandmother every weekend.
options.c: I would help if I could.

questions.explanation: 'would' + base verb = past habitual action (used to equivalent).

questions.subtopic: Modal verb used to past habit basic
questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'used to' for past habit?

options.a: I used to play in the park when I was young.
options.b: I used to plays in the park.
options.c: I used to playing in the park.
options.d: I am used to playing in the park now.

questions.explanation: 'used to' + base verb = past habit (no longer true).

questions.subtopic: Modal verb had better advice basic
questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'had better' correctly?

options.a: You had better study for the test.
options.c: You had better studying for the test.

questions.explanation: 'had better' + base verb = strong advice.

questions.subtopic: Modal verb ought to advice basic
questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'ought to' correctly?

options.a: You ought to apologize for being late.

questions.explanation: 'ought to' + base verb = moral obligation/advice.

questions.subtopic: Modal verb need to necessity basic
questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'need to' correctly?

options.a: I need to finish my homework before dinner.

questions.explanation: 'need to' + base verb = necessity.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'dare' correctly?

options.a: He dare not speak in public.

questions.explanation: 'dare not' + base verb = challenge/bravery negation.

questions.questionText: Which sentence gives a warning using first conditional?

options.a: If you touch that wire, you will get an electric shock.
options.b: If you touched that wire, you would get a shock.
options.c: If you had touched that wire, you would have got a shock.
options.d: If you touch wires, you get shocks.

questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present, will + base verb (real warning).

questions.questionText: Which sentence makes a promise using first conditional?

options.a: If you help me today, I will help you tomorrow.
options.b: If you helped me, I would help you.
options.c: If you had helped me, I would have helped you.
options.d: If you helps me, I help you.

questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present, will + base verb (real promise).

questions.questionText: Which sentence offers help using first conditional?

options.a: If you need any help, I will assist you.
options.b: If you needed help, I would assist you.
options.c: If you had needed help, I would have assisted.
options.d: If you need help, I assist you.

questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present, will + base verb (real offer).

questions.questionText: Which sentence gives advice about a hypothetical situation?

options.a: If I were you, I would study harder.
options.b: If I am you, I will study harder.
options.c: If I had been you, I would have studied harder.
options.d: If I be you, I study harder.

questions.explanation: Second conditional: If + were/Subjunctive past, would + base verb (advice).

questions.questionText: Which sentence describes an impossible dream?

options.a: If I could fly, I would visit every country.
options.b: If I can fly, I will visit every country.
options.c: If I had flown, I would have visited.
options.d: If I fly, I visit countries.

questions.explanation: Second conditional: If + could + base verb, would + base verb (unreal).

questions.questionText: Which sentence states a scientific fact using zero conditional?

options.a: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils.
options.b: If you heated water, it boiled.
options.c: If you had heated water, it would have boiled.
options.d: If you heat water, it will boil.

questions.explanation: Zero conditional: If + present, present (scientific fact).

questions.questionText: Which sentence describes an everyday routine using zero conditional?

options.a: If I wake up late, I miss the bus.
options.b: If I woke up late, I would miss the bus.
options.c: If I had woken up late, I would have missed the bus.
options.d: If I wake up late, I will miss the bus.

questions.explanation: Zero conditional: If + present, present (general routine).

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'They had finished the project.'

options.a: The project had been finished by them.
options.b: The project had finished by them.
options.c: The project was finished by them.
options.d: The project has been finished by them.

questions.explanation: Passive past perfect: had been + past participle.

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'They might repair the road.'
questions.explanation: Passive modal: modal + be + past participle.

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'They will complete the work tomorrow.'

options.a: The work will be completed tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Passive future: will be + past participle.

questions.questionText: Convert: 'I am working hard,' she said.

options.a: She said that she was working hard.
options.b: She said that she is working hard.
options.c: She said that I was working hard.
options.d: She says she was working hard.

questions.explanation: Reported speech: present continuous → past continuous.

questions.questionText: Convert: 'I have finished the work,' he said.

options.a: He said that he had finished the work.
options.b: He said that he has finished the work.
options.c: He said that he finished the work.
options.d: He said I had finished the work.

questions.explanation: Reported speech: present perfect → past perfect.

questions.questionText: Convert: 'I can help you,' she said.

options.a: She said that she could help me.
options.b: She said that she can help me.
options.c: She said that I could help.
options.d: She said she can help me.

questions.explanation: Reported speech: 'can' → 'could' (modal backshift).

questions.questionText: Identify the correct reflexive pronoun use.

options.a: The students helped each other with the homework.

questions.explanation: 'Each other' = reciprocal pronoun (used for two or more).

questions.questionText: Identify the correct reciprocal pronoun.

options.a: The twins looked at one another in surprise.
options.b: The twins looked at each for surprise.

questions.explanation: 'One another' = reciprocal (formal, for more than two).

questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'abundant'.
questions.explanation: Antonym of 'abundant' = 'scarce' (opposite meaning).

questions.questionText: Which pair of words has the closest meaning?
questions.explanation: 'Big' and 'large' = synonyms (similar meaning).

questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'as plain as day' mean?
questions.explanation: 'As plain as day' = very clear or obvious.

questions.questionText: What does 'a chip off the old block' mean?
questions.explanation: 'A chip off the old block' = behaves like parent.

questions.questionText: What does 'on cloud nine' mean?
questions.explanation: 'On cloud nine' = extremely happy or elated.

questions.questionText: What does 'learn by heart' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Learn by heart' = memorize completely.

questions.questionText: What does 'break the bank' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Break the bank' = spend or cost too much money.

questions.questionText: What does 'hit the road' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Hit the road' = begin a journey or trip.

questions.questionText: What does 'climb the career ladder' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Climb the career ladder' = advance in career.

questions.questionText: What does 'bring about' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Bring about' = cause something to happen.

questions.questionText: What does 'come across' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Come across' = find or meet by chance.

questions.questionText: What does 'depend on' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Depend on' = rely on or be decided by.

questions.questionText: What does 'hold on' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Hold on' = wait a moment.

questions.questionText: What does 'make up' mean in 'Let's make up the story'?
questions.explanation: 'Make up' = invent or create something new.

questions.questionText: Which word uses the suffix '-hood' to mean state/condition?
questions.explanation: 'Childhood' = state of being a child (-hood suffix).

questions.questionText: Read: 'Phone X: 6GB RAM, $300. Phone Y: 4GB RAM, $400.' What is compared?
questions.explanation: Comparison: Phone X (6GB, $300) vs Phone Y (4GB, $400).

questions.questionText: Read: 'NOTICE: Sports Day postponed to Friday due to rain. All students please assemble at the field.' What is this?
questions.explanation: Format: 'NOTICE' + event change = school announcement.

questions.questionText: Read: 'I believe online learning is the future. It offers flexibility for students worldwide.' What is the writer's opinion?
questions.explanation: Opinion: 'I believe' + 'is the future' = positive.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Marie Curie discovered radium in 1898. She won two Nobel Prizes for her work in physics and chemistry.' What is this about?
questions.explanation: Biography: life achievements of Marie Curie.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Visit Langkawi! White beaches, clear waters, sunset views. Packages from RM500 per person.' What is this?
questions.explanation: Brochure: destination description + price.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Dear Sir, I am writing to request information about your company's delivery services. Could you send me the details?' What is this?
questions.explanation: Format: 'Dear Sir' + 'writing to request' = formal request.

questions.questionText: Read: 'A tortoise challenged a hare to a race. The hare ran fast but rested. The tortoise kept going and won.' What is the moral?

options.a: Slow and steady wins the race.

questions.explanation: Moral: persistence and steady effort wins.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Name: ___ Age: ___ Address: ___ Signature: ___' What is this?
questions.explanation: Format: blank fields for personal info = application form.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Ingredients: wheat, sugar, salt. Best before: 2026. Store in cool place.' What is this?
questions.explanation: Format: ingredients + expiry = food label.

questions.questionText: Read: 'I strongly disagree with the new parking policy. It will harm small businesses.' What type of text is this?
questions.explanation: Format: 'I disagree' + reasoning = letter to editor.

questions.questionText: Read: 'TO: All staff. FROM: Manager. DATE: 15 March. SUBJECT: Meeting cancelled.' What is this?
questions.explanation: Format: TO/FROM/DATE/SUBJECT = memo.

questions.questionText: Read: 'The city council approved a new park yesterday. Construction begins in May.' What is the main event?
questions.explanation: Main event: 'council approved a new park'.

questions.questionText: Read: 'This novel is a masterpiece. The plot is gripping and the characters unforgettable.' What is this?
questions.explanation: Review: opinion + reasons (masterpiece, gripping).

questions.questionText: Read: 'Mon: 9am Math, 10am English. Tue: 9am Science, 10am History.' What is this?
questions.explanation: Format: days + times + subjects = schedule.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Step 1: Open the box. Step 2: Connect the cable. Step 3: Press the power button.' What is this?
questions.explanation: Format: numbered steps = user guide instructions.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'It rained. We went hiking.' (use 'although')

options.a: Although it rained, we went hiking.
options.b: It rained and we went hiking.
options.c: It rained but we went hiking.
options.d: It rained so we went hiking.

questions.explanation: 'Although' = concession (despite the rain).

questions.questionText: Combine: 'She was tired. She went to bed early.' (use 'because')

options.a: She went to bed early because she was tired.
options.b: She was tired and she went to bed early.
options.c: She was tired but went to bed early.
options.d: She was tired so went to bed.

questions.explanation: 'Because' = cause/reason.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'He is rich. He is unhappy.' (use 'but')
questions.explanation: 'But' = contrast.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'I was hungry. I ate a sandwich.' (use 'so')

options.a: I was hungry, so I ate a sandwich.
options.b: I was hungry and ate a sandwich.
options.c: I was hungry but ate a sandwich.
options.d: I was hungry because ate sandwich.

questions.explanation: 'So' = result/consequence.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'The bell rang. Students stood up.' (use 'when')

options.a: When the bell rang, students stood up.
options.b: The bell rang and students stood up.
options.c: The bell rang but students stood up.
options.d: The bell rang so students stood up.

questions.explanation: 'When' = at the time.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'She danced. He sang.' (use 'while')
questions.explanation: 'While' = simultaneous actions.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'It snows. Roads close.' (use 'if')
questions.explanation: 'If' = condition (zero conditional pattern).

questions.questionText: Find the error: 'I saw an elephant in a zoo.'

options.c: in a zoo → at a zoo

questions.explanation: 'An elephant' should be 'a elephant' (consonant sound).

questions.questionText: Find the error: 'She is good in Mathematics.'
questions.explanation: 'Good at Mathematics' (correct preposition).

questions.questionText: Find the error: 'Me and Tom went to the park.'
questions.explanation: Subject pronoun 'I' (not object 'me') before verb.

questions.questionText: Find the error: 'Yesterday I go to the park and play.'
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' requires past tense 'went'.

questions.questionText: Identify the sentence fragment.
questions.explanation: Fragment: dependent clause with no independent clause.

questions.questionText: Identify the parallel structure error: 'She likes swimming, to run, and biking.'
questions.explanation: Parallel: swimming / running / biking (all gerunds).

questions.questionText: Rearrange: 'always / She / breakfast / has / early'.
questions.explanation: Word order: Subject + adverb + verb + object + adverb.

questions.subtopic: Sentence transformation statement to question basic
questions.questionText: Transform to question: 'She is a teacher.'
questions.explanation: Yes/no question: 'Is' + subject + complement?

questions.questionText: Choose the polite reply to an email request.

options.a: Thank you for your email. I will send the information shortly.

questions.explanation: Polite email reply: thank + promise.

questions.questionText: Choose the email apology for a mistake.

options.a: I apologize for the error in my previous email. I have corrected it.

questions.explanation: Email apology: apologize + acknowledgment + correction.

questions.questionText: Choose the email thank you after a job interview.

options.a: Thank you for the interview opportunity. I enjoyed learning about the role.

questions.explanation: Thank you email: thank + positive comment.

questions.questionText: Choose the lost-and-found notice.

options.a: LOST: Black wallet near library on Monday. Contact Security Office.

questions.explanation: Lost-found notice: 'LOST' header + description + contact.

questions.questionText: Choose the essential content of a voice message.
questions.explanation: Voice message essentials: name + number + reason.

questions.questionText: Choose the polite birthday invitation.

options.a: You are cordially invited to my birthday party on Saturday at 7pm.

questions.explanation: Polite invitation: 'cordially invited' + date + time.

questions.questionText: Choose the sincere apology expression.

options.a: I sincerely apologize for my mistake. I will make sure it does not happen again.

questions.explanation: Sincere apology: apologize + reason + corrective action.

questions.questionText: Choose the thank you letter after someone helped you.

options.a: Thank you for helping me with my project. I really appreciate your time.

questions.explanation: Thank you letter: thanks + specific reason + appreciation.

questions.questionText: Choose the request for information formal letter opening.

options.a: I am writing to request information about your products and services.

questions.explanation: Formal request: 'I am writing to request information about'.

questions.questionText: Choose the formal complaint email opening.

options.a: I am writing to formally complain about the product I recently purchased.

questions.explanation: Formal complaint: 'I am writing to formally complain about'.

questions.questionText: What would you say when checking in at the airport?

options.a: I have a reservation under the name Lee.

questions.explanation: Airport checkin: 'I have a reservation under the name...'

questions.questionText: How would you buy a bus ticket?

options.a: One ticket to Kuala Lumpur, please.

questions.explanation: Bus ticket: 'One ticket to [destination], please.'

questions.questionText: How would you check in at a hotel?

options.a: I have a reservation. My name is Tan.

questions.explanation: Hotel checkin: 'I have a reservation. My name is...'

questions.questionText: How would you open a bank account?

options.a: I'd like to open a savings account, please.

questions.explanation: Bank: 'I'd like to open a savings account, please.'

questions.questionText: How would you ask for medicine at a pharmacy?

options.a: I'd like something for a headache, please.

questions.explanation: Pharmacy: 'I'd like something for a [symptom], please.'

questions.questionText: How would you report a theft to the police?

options.a: I'd like to report a theft that happened this morning.

questions.explanation: Police report: 'I'd like to report a theft that happened...'

questions.questionText: How would you report a lost item?

options.a: I've lost my bag. Could you help me, please?

questions.explanation: Lost item: 'I've lost my [item]. Could you help me, please?'

questions.questionText: How would you suggest a time for a meeting?
questions.explanation: Meeting time: 'Would [time] suit you?' = polite suggestion.

questions.questionText: How would you ask about today's weather?
questions.explanation: Weather: 'What's the weather like today?' = standard question.

questions.questionText: How would you start a casual conversation with someone new?

options.a: Hi, my name is Anna. What's yours?

questions.explanation: Small talk: 'Hi, my name is [X]. What's yours?'

questions.questionText: Read: 'The wind whispered through the trees.' What is this?
questions.explanation: 'Wind whispered' = giving human action to non-human (personification).

questions.questionText: Read: 'The bees buzzed in the garden.' What is this?
questions.explanation: 'Buzzed' = word imitating sound (onomatopoeia).

questions.questionText: Read: 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.' What is this?
questions.explanation: Alliteration: repetition of 'p' sound at beginning of words.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Her smile is like sunshine.' What is this?
questions.explanation: 'Like' = comparison (simile, not metaphor).

questions.questionText: Read a 4-line poem. Each set of lines is called?
questions.explanation: Stanza = group of lines in a poem.
